question: Angle subtended by a chord MN on the circumference of a circle is 90 degree. If diameter of the circle is 44 cm. then what will be the length of chord MN?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

By the **property of circles**, a chord subtends a 90° angle at the circumference if and only if it is the **diameter** of the circle.

Given **diameter** = 44 cm.

∴ The length of chord **MN** = 44 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 44 cm.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Diameter of the circle = 44 cm

Angle subtended by chord MN at the circumference = 90°

**Formula Used:**

**Angle in a semi-circle:** The angle subtended by the diameter of a circle at any point on its circumference is always 90°.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd6df84194e32cff2555710de7e24f88d02603567817efb2ac064f8738acbcf9.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let P be any point on the circumference of the circle.

⇒ Given that ∠MPN = 90°.

⇒ According to **Thales’ Theorem**, if an angle subtended by a chord at the circumference is a right angle, then that chord must be the **diameter** of the circle.

⇒ Chord MN = Diameter of the circle

⇒ MN = 44 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 44 cm.**

**__Additional Information__**

Thales' Theorem

It states that if M, N, and P are points on a circle where the line MN is a diameter, then the angle ∠MPN is a right angle (90°).

Chord and Central Angle

The central angle subtended by the diameter is 180°. Since the angle at the circumference is half the angle at the center, 180° ÷ 2 = 90°.

Longest Chord

The diameter is the longest possible chord in any circle and its length is twice the radius (D = 2 × r).</p
